content_html:
Bread freezes well and generally keeps better quality when frozen fresh, wrapped tightly, and divided into portions that can be used at one time. Slicing before freezing avoids thawing an entire loaf whenever only part is needed.

Freeze bread while it is still fresh

Freezing preserves the bread’s current state; it does not restore moisture or texture to a loaf that is already stale. Cool freshly baked bread completely before wrapping so condensation is not trapped.

Slice or portion before wrapping

Separate slices with paper if they tend to stick and freeze portions sized for normal use. This lets you remove only what you need without repeated thawing cycles.

Protect the bread from air to limit freezer burn

Use freezer-safe wrapping or a bag and remove excess air without crushing the bread. A second layer can help for longer storage, especially with crusty loaves that have a lot of exposed surface.

Thaw only the amount you plan to use

Slices can go directly to a toaster when the appliance allows it or thaw briefly at room temperature. For a larger loaf, keep it wrapped while it warms so moisture is not lost too quickly.
